headline: US legal cannabis sales hit record $2.6 billion in October
dek: Legal US cannabis sales reached about $2.60 billion in October across 29 markets, a monthly record that lifts 2026's ten-month total to $24.2 billion.
key_points: Legal cannabis sales in 23 adult-use states and six large medical markets reached about $2.60 billion in October, a monthly record, according to The Marijuana Herald's tally.
Daily sales held at about $84 million, flat on September: the record comes from October's extra day, not faster buying.
Six states (California, Michigan, New York, Massachusetts, Illinois and Missouri) took about 45% of the total, by MetaFlora's calculation.
Medical-only Pennsylvania outsold Massachusetts' combined adult-use and medical market, and medical-only markets made up nearly 18% of the month.
body: Americans bought about $2.60 billion of legal cannabis in October 2026, the largest monthly total recorded this year, according to an analysis by The Marijuana Herald published on 10 November. The figure covers all 23 states with operating adult-use markets plus six of the largest medical-only markets, and brings estimated sales for the first ten months of the year to $24.2 billion.

The record is real but modest. October's total was about 3% above September's $2.52 billion, and October had one more day. Measured per day, sales held at roughly $84 million, essentially unchanged. The national market is growing by adding states and stores, not by each customer spending faster, and prices continue to fall in mature markets.
## Where the money went

California remained the largest market at about $336.9 million, followed by Michigan at $244.4 million and New York at $173.7 million. Massachusetts reported about $154.7 million in combined adult-use and medical sales, Illinois $137.3 million and Missouri $134.1 million, according to the Herald's state-by-state table.

Together those six states sold about $1.18 billion, or 45.4% of the national total, by MetaFlora's calculation from the table. California alone accounted for 12.9%. Michigan's $244.4 million was about 72.5% of California's October total, and Michigan outsold New York by about $70.7 million.

Below the top six, Ohio sold about $121.4 million, Maryland $105.2 million, and Colorado, New Jersey and Arizona each sold close to $100 million. At the small end, Rhode Island recorded $10.56 million and Delaware an estimated $8.2 million.
> The record is a calendar effect: one extra day, not a faster customer. Growth now comes from new states and new stores.
## Medical-only markets still matter

The six medical-only markets in the tally (Florida, Pennsylvania, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Utah and Virginia) sold about $460.9 million between them, or 17.7% of the national figure. Pennsylvania's medical-only market alone sold $160.2 million, more than Massachusetts' entire adult-use and medical market. Florida, at an estimated $188.1 million, would rank third nationally if it were counted as a single state market, ahead of New York.

Those numbers explain why legalization fights in Pennsylvania and Florida draw so much industry money. As we reported on 6 November, Democrats won control of the Pennsylvania Senate, opening a path for adult-use legislation. Converting a $160 million monthly medical market into a broader adult-use one would add one of the largest markets in the country without creating a new customer base from scratch.
## How the estimate was built

The Herald's total combines newly released state regulator data with figures from analytics firm Headset, updated on 9 November. Where neither source had October numbers, the Herald estimated them from earlier monthly sales and national trends. Five markets are estimates in the table: Delaware, Florida, Oklahoma, Vermont and Virginia. Together they account for about $278.5 million, or 10.7% of the total, so the national figure could move when those states publish actual data.

State data carry their own caveats. Massachusetts, for example, publishes sales through the Cannabis Control Commission's open data platform, which notes that the figures are self-reported by licensees and may be revised. Other medical-only states were left out because they do not report sales often enough. The total is therefore a floor for the legal market, not a complete count. It also excludes hemp-derived THC products sold outside dispensaries, a category that faces new state and federal limits from 12 November and 11 December.
## The trend through 2026

Monthly totals in the Herald's series have moved in a narrow band this year: about $2.47 billion in June, $2.56 billion in July, $2.55 billion in August, $2.52 billion in September and $2.60 billion in October. August was about 12% higher than a year earlier, the Herald reported in September, but part of that growth came from markets that did not exist a year before, such as Minnesota and Delaware.

The ten-month total of $24.2 billion works out to about $2.42 billion a month. If November and December match October, full-year 2026 sales would land near $29.4 billion. That is MetaFlora's arithmetic, not a forecast: holiday demand, new store openings and further price cuts could each move the last two months in either direction.

State data released this week show the price pressure. In Connecticut, adult-use sales set a record $20.5 million in October while the average gram fell to $6.36, down about 25% in a year, as we reported on 10 November. More product at lower prices is the pattern across most mature markets.
## What it means for operators and investors

For multistate operators, flat daily sales and falling prices mean revenue growth depends on new licences, new states and cost control rather than rising demand per store. Relief from the Section 280E tax burden under rescheduling has cut some companies' tax bills, as Cresco Labs' results showed on 8 November, but it has not changed the basic price trend at the counter.

For states, the numbers show tax bases that are large but no longer growing quickly in the oldest markets. Missouri, which turns intoxicating hemp products into regulated marijuana from 12 November, is one market where a policy change could move the monthly total.
## What to watch

November figures will arrive from state regulators through early December. Watch Missouri for any shift from hemp shops into dispensaries after its hemp law takes effect, Pennsylvania for movement on adult-use legislation in the new session, and whether the estimated markets, led by Florida, confirm the Herald's numbers when official data are published.
